resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA list says Platform and the 1937 report calls it a 40 ft tower; the Illinois Country Living profile describes it as only a platform on a telephone pole, so the record keeps platform.

notes_for_editor: Height 12.2 m is converted from the 1937 report's 40 ft; the report does not say whether 40 ft is to the top of the pole or the platform. Staffing comes from a 1937 plan (John Rotes will man it), not a record of later service, so the staffing entry is weaker than the status shows. The 1938 National Archives photo (no. 364418) is credited in the Illinois Country Living caption, which was checked; the photo itself was not fetched, so no image URL is listed. The fire finder photo is implied by the Frakes wording as you can see at Melcher but was not located. The early-tower platform description is an Illinois Country Living statement, not a direct Frakes quote. The record's kind platform is kept rather than changed to tower. No removal date was found. The 1937 report also names a planned secondary tower at Benham Hill, Pope County; it is not covered here.
